items.title: Shell integration tests source the wrapper path without shell quoting
items.recommendation: Add a small shell-quoting helper for paths embedded in `bash -c` scripts, or avoid string interpolation by passing the script path as an argument/environment variable and sourcing `"$ANVIL_RUN_SCRIPT"`. Apply it consistently at all three call sites.
items.reproduction: Run the crate tests from a checkout path containing a space, or adjust the test to source a copied `anvil-run.sh` from a temp directory named with a space; the generated `. /path/with space/anvil-run.sh` command will not source the intended file.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests use the current `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, which usually has no whitespace or shell metacharacters, so the unquoted path bug is not exercised.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Copy `shell/anvil-run.sh` into a temp directory whose name contains a space, source that copied path through the same test helper, and assert the dispatcher still invokes the stub.
items.minimumFixScope: Change `crates/anvil-run/tests/shell_integration.rs` to quote or otherwise safely pass `script_path()` in all generated bash snippets.

items.title: Standalone daemon command is not covered by process-level tests
items.recommendation: Add a small process-level integration test for the binary contract, at minimum covering help/usage and invalid invocation. If feasible on Unix, also spawn `anvil-intercept start` under an isolated temporary HOME/state directory, send SIGTERM, and assert it exits successfully.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Both included test files construct `IpcListener` or service harnesses in-process, bypassing `crates/anvil-intercept/src/main.rs` entirely.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Use `CARGO_BIN_EXE_anvil-intercept` or an `assert_cmd` equivalent to verify `anvil-intercept --help`, `anvil-intercept` without a subcommand, and a Unix-only `anvil-intercept start` smoke test that terminates via SIGTERM in a temporary environment.
items.minimumFixScope: Add binary-level integration coverage for `crates/anvil-intercept/src/main.rs`; no daemon library changes are required.

items.title: Air-gapped status verification can still attempt network refresh before running the local probe
items.recommendation: Special-case local/offline status verification before silent refresh, or add an auth-check mode that refuses/returns auth-required without refresh for commands documented as air-gapped. Then run the air-gapped harness without `ANVIL_DEV` against an isolated expired credential fixture with a refresh token.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included air-gapped test bypasses auth with `ANVIL_DEV=1`, so it verifies the status command body but not the global auth layer that runs first in production.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend `air_gapped.rs` with a test that seeds isolated expired credentials containing a refresh token, runs `anvil --no-tui --json status --verify` through the network-blocked harness without `ANVIL_DEV`, and asserts the process does not attempt or hang on network refresh.
items.minimumFixScope: `crates/anvil-cli/src/main.rs` auth pre-dispatch policy for documented local/offline commands plus the air-gapped credential fixture test.

items.title: JSON-mode auth failures emit human text before the JSON error envelope
items.recommendation: Thread JSON/machine-output mode into auth evaluation, or make `check_auth` return a structured auth error without printing when `global.json` is set, leaving `main` as the single JSON error renderer.
items.reproduction: env -u ANVIL_DEV -u ANVIL_LICENSE ANVIL_NO_PROMPT=1 XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$(mktemp -d) cargo run -p eddacraft-anvil -- --json status 2>err; cat err
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included JSON-mode tests either use unauthenticated commands or set `ANVIL_DEV=1`, so they never exercise the gated auth-failure path in JSON mode.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration test that runs a gated command such as `anvil --json status` with isolated empty credentials and `ANVIL_NO_PROMPT=1`, then asserts stderr is exactly one parseable JSON object and contains no human auth guidance.
items.minimumFixScope: `crates/anvil-cli/src/main.rs` auth error rendering plus one auth-failure JSON integration test.

items.title: Benchmark reports can be overwritten by runs started in the same second
items.recommendation: Make report paths collision-resistant and non-clobbering, for example by including subsecond time plus process id or a UUID, and create the file with exclusive-create semantics so collisions fail instead of overwriting.
items.reproduction: Start two `cargo run -p anvil-bench --release -- graph_memory` processes from the same directory within the same Unix second; both compute the same `bench-results/stress-<timestamp>.json` output path and one report is lost.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests exercise the CLI entrypoint or concurrent/same-second output path generation; existing report serialization tests do not validate collision behaviour for main.rs.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration-style test around output path generation or a refactored `run` helper that forces the same timestamp for two runs and asserts the second run does not overwrite the first report.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the output filename/open mode in `crates/anvil-bench/src/main.rs`; factor path generation into a small testable helper if needed.

items.title: Root tsconfig lists files that TypeScript does not actually check
items.recommendation: Either remove the inert entries and keep this as a narrow TypeScript-only config check, or add a dedicated config-check tsconfig that enables `allowJs`/`checkJs` for eslint.config.mjs and uses the current E2E path, likely `apps/e2e/**/*` if root-level E2E files are still intended.
items.reproduction: `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit --explainFiles | rg 'eslint\.config|jest\.config|e2e|vitest\.config|playwright\.config'` only reports vitest.config.ts and playwright.config.ts as matched by tsconfig.json.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this config. The existing root TypeScript invocation succeeds because TypeScript silently ignores the unmatched or unsupported include entries.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a small validation script or test that runs `tsc --explainFiles` for the root config and asserts every intentional include entry is either matched or explicitly documented as inert.
items.minimumFixScope: Update tsconfig.json include entries and, if JS config checking is intended, the compilerOptions needed to make eslint.config.mjs part of the checked program.

items.title: Root Vitest discovery can miss package __tests__ directories outside src
items.recommendation: Add an include pattern for package __tests__ directories that are not necessarily under src, or align the documented convention and config so there is a single discoverable test location. Consider disabling passWithNoTests at the root config if CI expects the root suite to find tests.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests or config smoke tests are included that assert the Vitest include globs discover expected repository test locations.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a small config-level test or CI smoke check that uses Vitest's resolved config/glob matching to assert packages/example/__tests__/sample.test.ts and packages/example/src/sample.test.ts are both discoverable.
items.minimumFixScope: vitest.config.ts include globs and, if retained intentionally, an explicit documented rationale for passWithNoTests.

items.title: Node type definitions exceed the supported runtime contract
items.recommendation: Either align @types/node to the minimum supported Node major, or raise the engines.node minimum if Node 25 APIs are intentionally allowed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests exercise adapter parsing and serialization behavior; they do not verify package metadata consistency or run the suite against the minimum supported Node runtime.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package metadata validation test that checks the @types/node major does not exceed the minimum engines.node major, or add CI coverage on Node 22 that catches runtime use of newer Node APIs.
items.minimumFixScope: package.json devDependency or engines.node

items.title: Public crate docs still describe shipped validation as deferred
items.recommendation: Update the `lib.rs` scope/out-of-scope section to reflect that hard-pinned validation is now part of the crate, and explicitly state that `parse_str`/`parse_file` parse only while callers that load operator config should call `validate_hard_pinned_classes` after parsing.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests cover parse and validation behavior, but they do not verify that the public crate documentation matches the shipped API surface.
items.minimumFixScope: Documentation-only change in `crates/anvil-config/src/lib.rs`.

items.title: rule panic isolation is not valid in release builds with panic=abort
items.recommendation: Either build the daemon/rule-execution path with panic="unwind" if catch_unwind is the intended boundary, or move rule execution behind a process boundary so aborting rules cannot terminate the daemon. Add the documented multi-process release fixture before treating the contract as covered.
items.reproduction: Run the daemon in a release profile configured with panic="abort" and install a rule equivalent to panicking_rule_service; sending rule_panic_request aborts the daemon process instead of returning the unwind-mode empty diagnostics response.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current Rust fixture explicitly pins only panic="unwind" behaviour under cargo test and documents the panic="abort" release path as an unimplemented follow-up.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a multi-process release-profile test that starts the daemon with a panicking rule and asserts the expected release contract, either no daemon abort or a controlled child-process failure with daemon survival.
items.minimumFixScope: Release profile or rule-execution isolation strategy, plus the midedit_contract release-mode regression fixture.

items.title: stale PID recovery can remove a newly-created live PID file
items.recommendation: Serialise PID-file recovery and daemon ownership with an actual lock, or make recovery remove only the exact file identity that was inspected. On Unix, hold a lock file or locked open PID file across recovery and daemon lifetime; do not rely on a read/status/remove/create sequence alone.
items.reproduction: Start two run_foreground instances concurrently against the same stale PID file, with recovery interleaved so both read the stale record before either remove_file call completes. The second remover can unlink the first starter's replacement PID file.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover stale recovery and that Drop preserves an already-replaced PID file, but they do not run two stale-recovery attempts concurrently or force the interleaving between stale read, first recreate, and second remove.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Unix test that uses two coordinated tasks/processes and an injected recovery hook to pause both after stale-status detection, then lets one recreate the PID file before the other attempts removal. Assert the live replacement is not removed and only one daemon proceeds.
items.minimumFixScope: PidFileGuard acquisition and stale PID recovery logic in crates/anvil-intercept/src/lib.rs, plus a targeted concurrent stale-recovery regression test.

items.title: Top-level rustdoc incorrectly says the 80-writer stress test is ignored
items.recommendation: Update the `crates/anvil-witness/src/lib.rs` deferred follow-up text to match the current test state, or remove the deferred follow-up entirely if MLP2-015 completed it.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests exercise writer concurrency behaviour, but they do not validate rustdoc accuracy or cross-document consistency.
items.minimumFixScope: Edit the stale crate-level documentation in `crates/anvil-witness/src/lib.rs`.

items.title: scan_artifact_json does not catch registry-load panics
items.recommendation: Move the registry load into the same catch_unwind block as scan_artifact_rust, or wrap the whole scan_artifact_json implementation after JSON argument validation so registry panics are converted through panic_to_error.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The referenced registry-missing test covers ordinary load errors returned as Result values, but it does not exercise a panic from registry loading or mapping on scan_artifact_json.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Node integration test or Rust-side injectable loader test that forces the scan entrypoint's registry-load path to panic and asserts scanArtifactJson throws a JS Error instead of aborting the process.
items.minimumFixScope: crates/anvil-checks-napi/src/lib.rs scan_artifact_json panic boundary

items.title: Pool cap behaviour is not covered by the library test
items.recommendation: Add a regression test that validates the cap in an isolated process before any other rayon consumer can initialise the global pool. If direct global-pool testing is too fragile for unit tests, factor the cap calculation into a small pure helper and test that helper, then add one integration or subprocess smoke test for `init_global` applying it first.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The sole included test only calls `init_global()` twice and asserts no panic by implication; its own comment states that it does not assert the resulting thread count.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Run a subprocess or dedicated integration binary that calls `eddacraft_anvil_rayon_init::init_global()` before any `par_iter`, then asserts `rayon::current_num_threads() == (num_cpus::get() / 2).max(1)`.
items.minimumFixScope: Add focused coverage for the cap calculation and first-initialisation behaviour in `crates/anvil-rayon-init`.

items.title: Trace file creation can follow a raced symlink before validation
items.recommendation: Open trace files with no-follow semantics on Unix, for example OpenOptionsExt::custom_flags(libc::O_NOFOLLOW) plus create_new(true) for the absent-file path or an openat-style flow. Keep the post-open inode check, but make the open itself refuse symlinks.
items.reproduction: On Unix, set ANVIL_TRACE_SINK=file=<path in attacker-writable directory>. Race creation of <path> as a symlink after validate_existing_trace_file observes NotFound but before OpenOptions::open runs. The function can open the symlink target before returning TraceSink.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included Unix tests cover existing non-regular paths and private regular files, but they do not exercise the missing-path creation case or a symlink substitution race.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Unix test for a missing path where the final path is a symlink at open time, and assert open_trace_file returns an error without creating or opening the symlink target. If deterministic race injection is hard, factor the open path to make the NotFound-to-open transition testable.
items.minimumFixScope: crates/anvil-observability/src/lib.rs open_trace_file Unix opening flags and corresponding Unix tests.

items.title: Eval silently drops all but the first Rego query expression/result
items.recommendation: Either narrow the API contract by validating/rejecting multi-result, multi-expression, or binding queries, or change EvalResult to expose the full query result shape needed by downstream callers.
items.reproduction: Evaluate a query such as `x = [1, 2, 3][_]` or `1 + 2; 3 + 4`; the facade can only return the first expression from the first result and cannot represent the remaining rows/expressions/bindings.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tests cover construction, a single scalar rule, and undefined versus explicit null only; none exercise multi-expression queries, binding queries, or queries that produce more than one result row.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests for `1 + 2; 3 + 4` and `x = [1, 2, 3][_]`, asserting either a clear error for unsupported query shapes or preservation of every result/expression/binding.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `Engine::eval` result handling and tests in `crates/anvil-policy-engine/src/lib.rs`.

items.title: QueryStatus serializes to an undocumented command name instead of the documented JSON-RPC method
items.recommendation: Do not expose QueryStatus through the serializable command-envelope enum unless the daemon accepts that wire shape. Either remove/split the variant from the serde wire enum, add a custom serde implementation that rejects command-envelope QueryStatus, or add an explicit supported route and tests for the `query-status` command form.
items.reproduction: Construct `IpcEnvelope::request("req", IpcCommand::QueryStatus)` and serialize it with serde_json; it produces a command-envelope frame containing `"command":"query-status"`, not a JSON-RPC frame with `"method":"query_status"`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The test module covers list-sessions, unblock-cascade, unblock-worktree, and unknown commands, but has no test that serializes or deserializes IpcCommand::QueryStatus or checks it against the documented `query_status` JSON-RPC method contract.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a proto test asserting that QueryStatus cannot be serialized as a command-envelope frame, or, if command-envelope support is intended, add a round-trip test that pins `{"command":"query-status"}` and pair it with daemon routing coverage for that exact frame.
items.minimumFixScope: Adjust the QueryStatus representation in `crates/anvil-intercept-proto/src/lib.rs` and add a focused serialization/deserialization test for the chosen contract.

items.title: Named-pipe EOF is surfaced as an OS error despite the documented Ok(0) contract
items.recommendation: Map the expected pipe EOF condition, at least ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE and any other documented named-pipe EOF status used by this handle mode, to Ok(0). Keep other ReadFile failures as io::Error::last_os_error().
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included client/server test writes a payload and reads it back before shutdown; it never closes the server side before the client read, so the ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE path is untested.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Windows test that creates an owner-only pipe server, connects a client, accepts the connection, drops or shuts down the server without writing, then asserts client.read(&mut buf) returns Ok(0).
items.minimumFixScope: OwnerOnlyPipeClient::read plus a focused Windows EOF regression test.

items.title: Root lint command mutates Markdown files during validation
items.recommendation: Make scripts.lint non-mutating by removing --fix or delegating to pnpm run lint:check. Keep auto-fixing behind lint:md:fix or a dedicated lint:fix script.
items.reproduction: Introduce an auto-fixable markdownlint violation in a tracked Markdown file, run pnpm lint, and observe that markdownlint rewrites the file instead of failing the validation command.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise adapter parsing, detection, serialization, and edge cases. None assert package script contracts or that validation commands leave the worktree unchanged.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a script-contract test that parses package.json and asserts scripts.lint does not contain known write flags such as --fix, while scripts ending in :fix may contain them.
items.minimumFixScope: Update package.json scripts.lint to use the non-fixing markdownlint invocation.

items.title: SURFENV-003 fixture test does not assert two expected findings by key or indicator
items.recommendation: Assert the exact expected finding set, for example by comparing keys and indicators for DATABASE_URL/prod host, FEATURE_FLAGS_ENV/production value, SECRET_PROD/key suffix, and LEGACY_HOST/suppressed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing assertions leave two of the four documented positive cases implicit behind findings.len() == 4.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Update prod_in_local_fixture_yields_expected_findings to assert the expected key/indicator/suppressed tuple set for all four findings.
items.minimumFixScope: Tighten assertions in crates/anvil-checks/tests/surfenv_prod_value.rs.

items.title: Only the first diagnostic is validated as a diagnostic envelope payload
items.recommendation: Iterate over every diagnostic and assert the required payload fields and category type for each one, then collect categories with a hard failure on missing or non-string values.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current test validates one representative diagnostic and uses `filter_map`, which skips malformed category fields instead of failing.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Change the diagnostic assertions to loop over `diagnostics.iter().enumerate()` and assert `schema_version`, `mode`, `id`, `severity`, `summary`, `category`, `source.rule_id`, `source.source_module`, and `location.file` for every element.
items.minimumFixScope: Strengthen the assertions in `crates/anvil-cli/tests/ai_guardrail_profile.rs` so all returned diagnostics are validated.

items.title: AI profile integration test does not verify the process exit status
items.recommendation: Assert the expected blocking exit behaviour explicitly, for example by checking `!output.status.success()` and comparing `parsed["exit_code"]` to `output.status.code()` when available.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current assertions parse stdout and validate the envelope shape, but they do not inspect `output.status` after the command completes.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend `ai_profile_emits_diagnostic_envelope_in_json_mode` to assert that the empty-workspace AI profile exits non-zero and that the envelope exit_code equals the process exit code.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `crates/anvil-cli/tests/ai_guardrail_profile.rs` to validate process status alongside the JSON envelope exit_code.

items.title: Watcher integration test uses a shorter readiness window despite known slow watcher registration
items.recommendation: Use a shared watcher-test helper with the same conservative readiness strategy for both tests, or create a sentinel parseable file and wait until it is observed before starting the actual assertion scenario. At minimum, align the warm-up and recv_timeout values with the more conservative test.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This is itself a test-suite reliability issue. The current assertions only verify behaviour when the OS watcher is already ready quickly enough; they do not make readiness deterministic.
items.minimumFixScope: Update crates/anvil-kernel/tests/watcher_integration.rs to use a common watcher startup/wait helper or consistent conservative timing for all OS watcher integration tests.

items.title: Explicit-any test would pass duplicate or spurious AP-003 detections
items.recommendation: Assert the exact number of AP-003 warnings for this fixture, and ideally assert distinct source lines or spans for the three expected occurrences.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Other tests assert broad totals for simpler fixtures, but this realistic-service test is the one covering multiple AP-003 occurrences in real TypeScript shape and it does not guard against over-reporting.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Change the assertion to expect exactly three AP-003 warnings and verify they correspond to the cache field, Promise return type, and cast lines.
items.minimumFixScope: Tighten the AP-003 assertion in detects_explicit_any_in_realistic_service.

items.title: Empty-catch detection lacks a non-empty catch negative test
items.recommendation: Add a negative integration test with one or more non-empty catch blocks and assert that AP-006 is absent for those cases.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Existing tests include a positive empty-catch case and clean code without catch blocks, but no handled catch block that exercises the false-positive boundary.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test such as scan_file("src/api/client.ts", "try { work(); } catch (err) { logger.error(err); throw err; }", None) and assert no warning with id AP-006 is present.
items.minimumFixScope: Extend crates/anvil-checks/tests/antipattern_scanning.rs with a non-empty catch negative case.

items.title: Test still inherits explicit Git repository environment
items.recommendation: Remove explicit Git environment from both Command invocations, at least GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE, and consider using env_clear with a small allowlist if the CLI does not need the broader parent environment.
items.reproduction: Run the integration test with an explicit inherited Git repository environment, for example from a real repository: `GIT_DIR=/path/to/repo/.git cargo test -p anvil-cli --test doctor_missing_git`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests only cover ancestor .git discovery via HOME and GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES. They do not cover inherited explicit Git environment variables because the Command setup leaves the rest of the parent environment intact.
items.minimumFixScope: Update both test Command builders in crates/anvil-cli/tests/doctor_missing_git.rs to clear explicit Git repository environment before invoking anvil.

items.title: Optional runner env file is omitted from the gitignore hygiene check when absent
items.recommendation: Keep absent optional env paths in the hygiene input with empty content, or add a separate path-only assertion that the configured gitignore patterns cover every gitignored path in `ANVIL_ENV_FILES`. Required committed templates should still fail if absent.
items.reproduction: On a checkout without `.github/actions-runner/.env`, remove the relevant `.env` or `.github/actions-runner` ignore coverage and run the SURFENV-002 test; the missing file is filtered out before hygiene checking.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The only hygiene test builds its `env_files` list through `filter_map`, so it never asserts that absent local-only paths are checked for ignore coverage.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a case that calls the hygiene baseline with `.github/actions-runner/.env` absent and a `.gitignore` that does not cover it, and assert an unsuppressed SURFENV-002 finding is produced.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `surfenv_002_gitignore_hygiene_is_clean_on_anvil` input construction or add a focused helper assertion for gitignored baseline paths.

items.title: Synthetic external smoke does not exercise positive SURFENV-001 detection
items.recommendation: Add an adversarial synthetic env value that deterministically triggers SURFENV-001 with entropy disabled, then assert at least one unsuppressed SURFENV-001 finding from `scan_env_file`.
items.reproduction: Change `scan_env_file` to return an empty list for all inputs, then run this integration test. The clean baseline assertions still pass and the synthetic smoke has no SURFENV-001 positive assertion to fail.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing SURFENV-001 test is a negative baseline only, and the synthetic positive smoke omits the secret scanner despite claiming to exercise every rule.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend `external_validation_smoke_against_synthetic_repo` with a known secret fixture and assert `scan_env_file(..., &config_no_entropy())` returns an unsuppressed SURFENV-001 finding for it.
items.minimumFixScope: Add one positive SURFENV-001 assertion to the synthetic smoke test.

items.title: Template drift test can pass vacuously when no drift findings are emitted
items.recommendation: Assert that each checked template with keys produces at least one unsuppressed finding, or assert the exact expected missing keys for the current templates.
items.reproduction: Make `check_env_drift` return an empty vector for template/concrete pairs, then run this test; it still passes as long as at least one `.example` file is readable.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The test's only non-vacuous guard counts checked template files, not generated drift findings.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: For the template-only pairwise run, collect the unsuppressed findings and assert it contains expected keys such as `DATABASE_URL` before checking their `MissingFromConcrete` kind.
items.minimumFixScope: Strengthen `surfenv_004_drift_check_template_only_pairwise_run_is_missing_from_concrete_only` with a non-empty or exact-key assertion.

items.title: Timeout regression is only tested on the successful handshake path
items.recommendation: Add a negative timeout integration test using an installed MCP entry whose command hangs or never emits a JSON-RPC initialize response, then assert `status --verify` returns within the expected budget plus tight CI slack and does not promote the client.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: `probe_is_skipped_when_no_install_yet` covers the absent-config gate, and the timed test covers only the happy path with `ANVIL_BIN`; neither exercises a configured but non-responsive child process.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create a temp executable or script that sleeps/blocks on stdio, install it as the configured MCP command, run `anvil status --verify`, assert elapsed time stays bounded, and assert the client remains unpromoted.
items.minimumFixScope: Extend `crates/anvil-cli/tests/spawn_probe.rs` with one negative timeout case.

items.title: Runtime exclude test does not exercise a violation-producing change
items.recommendation: Make the runtime write use a fixture that would emit a violation when unfiltered, or add a paired control in the same test/suite showing the same runtime change emits a violation without `exclude_patterns`. Then assert that only the excluded configuration suppresses it.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing test only asserts absence of vendor violation events after writing a benign file, so it does not prove the exclude predicate was applied to a violation-producing runtime event.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a no-exclude control for the same `vendor/lib/added.ts` contents and assert it produces a vendor violation, then keep the exclude case asserting it does not.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `excluded_runtime_change_does_not_emit_violation` and its fixture content/control assertion in `crates/anvil-kernel/tests/watch_pattern_filter.rs`.

items.title: Test counts clean JSON lines but does not verify every writer's record survived
items.recommendation: Collect parsed WitnessLine values and assert that the observed seq or commit_sha set exactly matches the expected values for all thread IDs.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The parser loop discards the parsed WitnessLine value and increments only a count, so identity and uniqueness of appended records are not checked.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: After parsing, build a set of commit_sha values and compare it with {t0-1, t1-2, ..., tN-1-N}.
items.minimumFixScope: Extend the existing parse loop in run_concurrent to retain parsed lines and assert expected unique writer IDs.

items.title: Concurrency test does not force simultaneous append contention
items.recommendation: Add an Arc<Barrier> shared by all worker threads and the main thread, have workers wait before calling append, then release them together after all handles are spawned.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Both test cases call the same run_concurrent helper, so neither variant guarantees overlapping append attempts.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Keep the existing 16/80 writer cases but gate the append call behind a Barrier so all spawned threads contend at once.
items.minimumFixScope: Update run_concurrent in crates/anvil-witness/tests/concurrency.rs to synchronise thread start before append.

items.title: Bare-exclude JSON stream test can pass without any stdout event
items.recommendation: After parsing, assert that the captured envelopes contain `WatchEventType::Snapshot`, or assert that `lines` includes the matching snapshot before checking stderr routing.
items.reproduction: Make the CLI return after printing the bare-exclude warning, before emitting a snapshot. As long as stderr contains a warn indicator, `vendor`, and `vendor/**`, this test reaches `parse_envelopes(&[], ...)` and passes.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The sibling test asserts snapshots only for the bare watch path without `--exclude`; this test's warning path only verifies stderr content and that any collected stdout lines parse.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Update `watch_json_stdout_carries_only_ndjson_when_bare_exclude_warning_present` to parse envelopes and assert at least one `Snapshot` event is present.
items.minimumFixScope: Add a snapshot/non-empty assertion in the bare-exclude integration test.

items.title: Invalid fenced JSON examples in public docs are silently ignored
items.recommendation: Return a `Result` from `extract_json_blocks` or panic with the block content/location when a fenced `json` block fails to parse.
items.reproduction: Add a malformed fenced `json` block to `docs/public/anvil/integrations/watch-output.md` while leaving the valid fixture examples intact. `public_docs_examples_match_fixtures` still passes because the malformed block is omitted from `documented_examples`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The only consumer, `public_docs_examples_match_fixtures`, checks that fixture values are contained in the successfully parsed examples; it does not verify that all fenced JSON blocks parsed successfully.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a small unit test for `extract_json_blocks` with malformed fenced JSON and assert it fails instead of silently returning fewer examples.
items.minimumFixScope: Change `extract_json_blocks` to treat parse errors in `json` fences as test failures.

items.title: Windows build excludes every positive violation assertion
items.recommendation: Add at least one Windows-compatible positive real-binary assertion, or gate only the path-sensitive cases and keep a platform-neutral positive case such as coverage_min below threshold active on Windows once the executor/path handling is fixed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The cfg attributes remove the positive cases from Windows builds, and the pass cases do not prove that violations can be produced and extracted there.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: On Windows, run a real OPA evaluation that should emit a coverage_min violation for 50 percent coverage and assert that the violation is present.
items.minimumFixScope: Narrow or remove the three #[cfg(not(target_os = "windows"))] guards after adding a Windows-safe positive violation fixture.

items.title: coverage_min_passes_at_threshold does not test the threshold boundary
items.recommendation: Change this test to use 80, or add a separate exact-threshold test while keeping the high-coverage case if desired.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current test only exercises a value well above the default threshold, so equality at the boundary is never asserted here.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Set input["context"]["coverage"] to {"lines": 80} and assert that no coverage_min violation is returned.
items.minimumFixScope: Update crates/anvil-policy/tests/opa_real_binary.rs in coverage_min_passes_at_threshold, or add one adjacent test for the exact 80 percent boundary.

items.title: Idempotence guard can pass even when verify fails or mutates HOME
items.recommendation: Assert both invocations succeed and still render the expected state, then snapshot the isolated home directory as well as the workdir before and after the verify runs.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing test ignores `Output.status` and only compares `snapshot(dir.path())`; it never inspects the returned status/stdout and never snapshots `home.path()`.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend `status_verify_is_idempotent_and_does_not_mutate_workdir` to assert success/state for each output and compare a second snapshot over `home.path()` before and after the two verify invocations.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the idempotence integration test in `crates/anvil-cli/tests/status_verify.rs`.

items.title: Auth-failure test depends on host networking state
items.recommendation: Avoid a magic external port. Bind a local TcpListener to port 0 for a deterministic test double, or use an explicitly invalid/unroutable endpoint only if the CLI contract maps that exact failure mode to authentication_required across platforms.
items.reproduction: Run the test on a host with a listener on 127.0.0.1:9, then execute `cargo test -p anvil-cli --test init_post_analysis json_verbose_edict_auth_failure_emits_only_json_error`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current test is itself the coverage, but it only validates the common case where localhost port 9 is closed; it does not control the network endpoint it relies on.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Replace the fixed API URL with a deterministic local test server or controlled failing endpoint, then assert the same single-line JSON error envelope.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `json_verbose_edict_auth_failure_emits_only_json_error` to remove the dependency on fixed localhost port 9.

items.title: Fixture update mode is racy under the default Rust test harness
items.recommendation: Make update mode single-owner and deterministic: either combine generation and verification into one test, skip round-trip verification while updating, use a serial test guard, or document and enforce `-- --test-threads=1` for fixture regeneration. Prefer atomic write-to-temp-then-rename if tests can ever read while updating.
items.reproduction: Run `ANVIL_UPDATE_FIXTURES=1 cargo test -p eddacraft-anvil --test status_render` with default test threading after deleting or adding a fixture path; `every_fixture_round_trips_through_protection_claim` can race the producer tests.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The suite itself contains the race and normally runs with committed fixtures, so the timing issue is only exposed during regeneration or variant additions.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an update-mode path that regenerates all fixtures before any verification reads them, or run this integration test with a serialisation guard and assert the documented update command succeeds from a clean fixture directory.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `crates/anvil-cli/tests/status_render.rs` to serialise fixture update/read phases or skip readers during `ANVIL_UPDATE_FIXTURES`.

items.title: Any ANVIL_UPDATE_FIXTURES value disables fixture assertions
items.recommendation: Require the environment variable to equal `1` exactly, and panic or ignore any other value so accidental configuration cannot turn golden assertions into fixture rewrites.
items.reproduction: Run `ANVIL_UPDATE_FIXTURES=0 cargo test -p eddacraft-anvil --test status_render`; fixture comparisons are bypassed because `var_os(...).is_some()` is true.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: There is no test around the update-mode gate itself; all callers share the same permissive helper.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a helper-level test or refactorable predicate test that asserts only `ANVIL_UPDATE_FIXTURES=1` enables fixture rewriting and values like `0`, `false`, and empty strings still compare fixtures.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the update-mode predicate in `assert_or_update_fixture` and keep the existing fixture comparison flow unchanged.

items.title: Busy test is hard-coded to two in-flight scan requests despite using a configurable limit
items.recommendation: Spawn MAX_CONCURRENT_SCAN_BUFFERS client tasks in a loop, store their handles, wait until all are blocking, then assert the busy response and release/join all handles generically.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current test happens to match the present limit, so it does not exercise the fixture against other valid values of MAX_CONCURRENT_SCAN_BUFFERS.
items.minimumFixScope: Refactor scan_buffer_busy_returns_structured_server_error in crates/anvil-intercept/tests/jsonrpc_conformance.rs to derive the number of in-flight clients from MAX_CONCURRENT_SCAN_BUFFERS.

items.title: Connection-liveness claim is not actually asserted
items.recommendation: After the no-response timeout, recover the client, write a normal request such as session.list with an id on the same stream, read one line, and assert the expected JSON-RPC result before shutting down.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This test only checks absence of a response within 150 ms; it never sends or reads the subsequent same-connection request described by its own fixture comments.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend oversized_scan_buffer_notification_is_dropped_silently to send {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session.list","id":"after-oversized-notification"} on the recovered stream and assert a result response with the same id.
items.minimumFixScope: Update crates/anvil-intercept/tests/jsonrpc_conformance.rs only.

items.title: Capped run over-reports scanned file count
items.recommendation: Move the cap check before incrementing files_scanned, or change the condition to break before counting/scanning once files_scanned has already reached 500.
items.reproduction: Run the test with ANVIL_DISCOVERY_REPRO=1 and ANVIL_DISCOVERY_REPRO_CAP_500=1 in a repository with more than 500 eligible source files; the summary can print files_scanned as 501 while scanner findings only cover the first 500 files.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This file is itself a gated manual repro test and has no assertions validating the summary counters under the capped mode.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a small unit-testable helper for the cap/counting behaviour and assert that capped scans report exactly the number of files actually scanned.
items.minimumFixScope: Adjust the counter/cap ordering inside discovery_repro_scan.

items.title: Claimed resolution-chain coverage is absent from the integration entrypoint
items.recommendation: Add deterministic tests for the strategy order itself. If full integration is impractical because `current_exe()` is hard to spoof, extract a small strategy resolver that accepts the executable path and sidecar lookup inputs, then test package-manager precedence, adjacent sidecar precedence over PATH sidecar, and library fallback when neither is present.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test in this file creates or simulates a package-manager-owned binary path, a sidecar binary, PATH sidecar discovery, or the library-fallback selection boundary. The existing assertions are about CLI surface flags and fixture formatting.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A table-driven resolver test covering package-manager -> adjacent sidecar -> PATH sidecar -> library fallback priority, plus one CLI-level smoke test for a mocked sidecar if the command can be made deterministic.
items.minimumFixScope: Introduce controllable resolution inputs or a small pure resolver function, then add tests that fail on priority-order regressions.

items.title: `--check --insecure-skip-verify` tests are not exercising the intended update verification behaviour
items.recommendation: Replace these with a deterministic parser-level test for the hidden flag and a direct test of the update verification preflight or a mocked library-fallback path that asserts stderr contains the loud `WARNING` text when verification is skipped. Avoid using the real `update --check` network/update probe as a parser surrogate.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing assertions only check `code != 2` and `status.code().is_some()`. They never assert that the skip-verify branch ran, that stderr contains the warning, or that the command stayed offline.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a unit test around the clap parser that accepts `update --check --insecure-skip-verify`, plus a test that calls the verification-skip path with `insecure_skip_verify=true` and captures/asserts the warning lines.
items.minimumFixScope: Adjust the update tests or update module test hooks so hidden-flag parsing and skip-verification warning emission are tested separately without invoking the real update check.

items.title: Suppressed fixture path is not checked for finding kind
items.recommendation: Add assertions for the suppressed finding's kind and suggested_pattern, mirroring the .env.local checks.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This test only validates kind and suggested_pattern for the unsuppressed local finding; the suppressed production finding has no equivalent assertions.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend fixture_repo_yields_one_unignored_finding_and_one_suppressed with assert_eq!(prod.kind, GitignoreFindingKind::UnignoredEnvFile) and assert_eq!(prod.suggested_pattern, ".env.production").
items.minimumFixScope: Update crates/anvil-checks/tests/surfenv_gitignore_hygiene.rs assertions for the .env.production finding.

items.title: Nested wrapper provenance can regress without failing this suite
items.recommendation: Assert the full expected nested wrapper chain for the parsed rm command, preferably in order, e.g. ["sudo", "bash"].
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The surrounding wrapper tests cover single wrappers exactly, but this is the only nested sudo+bash case and it explicitly weakens the assertion with an OR.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Change unwraps_nested_sudo_bash to assert_eq!(rm.wrapper_chain, vec!["sudo", "bash"]) or equivalent order-aware validation.
items.minimumFixScope: Update crates/anvil-checks/tests/command_safety_validation.rs only.

items.title: git clean -f expectation is internally inconsistent
items.recommendation: Pick one intended behaviour for git clean -f. If the intended default is Warn, make warns_on_git_clean_f assert CommandAction::Warn exactly; if Block is acceptable, loosen or parameterise the score test so it does not encode a contradictory contract.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The suite covers git clean -f in both places, but the assertions encode different acceptable behaviours rather than a single contract.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Assert the exact expected action for git clean -f at the rule-matching level and derive the mixed-score fixture from commands with fixed known actions.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the git clean assertions in crates/anvil-checks/tests/command_safety_validation.rs.

items.title: Audit hard-codes current SURFENV rules, so new rules can bypass it
items.recommendation: Drive this audit from a single SURFENV rule registry, or add an explicit coverage table that fails when the registered SURFENV rule count exceeds the audited cases. Include suppression mode metadata so every line-level and header-level rule gets a positive suppression case and at least one wrong-rule negative case.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The owned test is the audit, but its coverage is manually enumerated and has no assertion that all SURFENV rules are represented.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Expose a SURFENV_RULES registry from the surface env module, then assert the audit case table covers every registered rule_id exactly once and includes a wrong-rule suppression case for each suppression mode.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the test support/API to provide a canonical list of SURFENV structural rules, then refactor surfenv_suppression_audit.rs to assert audit coverage against that list.

items.title: Current-version contract is documented but not asserted
items.recommendation: Compare `parsed["current_version"]` to the expected crate/package version available to the integration test, rather than only checking that it is non-empty.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing test verifies key presence and basic shape, but it does not validate the specific version value promised by the test comment.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Assert `parsed["current_version"].as_str() == Some(env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"))` if that is the intended source of truth for the binary version.
items.minimumFixScope: Strengthen the assertion in `version_offline_json_keys_are_stable`.

items.title: Auth-gate regression test still inherits auth credentials from the parent environment
items.recommendation: Explicitly remove the known Anvil auth-related environment variables for this command, or use `env_clear()` and then add only the minimal variables needed for the binary to execute in the test environment.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The only auth-focused test starts the process without calling `.env(...)`, but that does not create an auth-free environment in Rust; it only avoids adding new variables.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Update `version_offline_does_not_require_auth` so it strips all known auth env vars before spawning `anvil`, then keep asserting success.
items.minimumFixScope: Adjust the integration test command setup in `crates/anvil-cli/tests/version_offline.rs`.

items.title: Human output test does not bind coverage tiers to the matching language
items.recommendation: Assert the association between each language and its expected tier, for example by matching full output rows/lines or by isolating the languages block and checking that the TypeScript row contains supported and the Python row contains unsupported.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current assertions are independent substring checks rather than row- or block-level assertions.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Tighten human_render_shows_per_language_breakdown so it fails when TypeScript and Python tier labels are swapped in the human renderer.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the human render integration test assertions in crates/anvil-cli/tests/status_verify_languages.rs.

items.title: Unclassified-file test allows overcounting to pass
items.recommendation: Make the expected count precise for this fixture, or add a second assertion that classified language files do not affect unclassified_files_seen. If .anvilrc is intentionally counted or ignored, encode that decision explicitly in the expected value.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current assertion checks presence and numeric type plus a minimum value, not counting accuracy or exclusion of classified files.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add multiple classified source files while keeping the same unclassified files and assert unclassified_files_seen remains the intended exact count.
items.minimumFixScope: Tighten unclassified_files_surface_in_json_output in crates/anvil-cli/tests/status_verify_languages.rs.

items.title: Vendored-directory regression test does not exercise the documented .git exclusion
items.recommendation: Add a source-like file under .git, such as .git/hooks/pre-commit.py or .git/objects/example.rs, and assert that it does not produce a Python or Rust language entry or increase files_seen.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current fixture never creates any file beneath .git, so the .git branch of the denylist is not covered.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend vendored_dirs_are_excluded_from_language_count with a .git-contained source file and assert it is ignored.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the vendored directory integration test fixture and assertions.

items.title: Claude Code missing-type test can pass for the wrong reason
items.recommendation: Make the fixture command match the default expected command, or pass --command /tmp/fake/anvil during verification, so the only failing condition is the missing type field.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The nearby JSON test covers a wrong type value, not the missing-type case; this test is the missing-type case but currently has a second independent failure condition.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Update mcp_install_verify_claude_code_requires_stdio_type so the configured command matches the verifier expectation while the type field remains absent.
items.minimumFixScope: Adjust the fixture or verify arguments in crates/anvil-cli/tests/mcp_config.rs.

items.title: Non-object config refusal tests do not verify the original file survives
items.recommendation: Read the config file after the failed install and assert it remains byte-identical to the seeded non-object JSON.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: write_refuses_when_existing_config_is_invalid_json checks preservation for invalid JSON, but these non-object JSON cases only check process status.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Capture the seeded JSON string before invoking install, then assert fs::read_to_string(path) equals that string after the failed command for both non-object cases.
items.minimumFixScope: Add post-failure file preservation assertions to the two non-object config tests.

items.title: Graph edge round-trip test permits a dangling target endpoint
items.recommendation: Create both source and target nodes, round-trip them with the edge, and assert that both edge_back.from and edge_back.to are present in the deserialised node id set.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current test only verifies the from endpoint and never materialises or validates the node with id 20.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Update graph_types_round_trip_together to include a second SymbolNode with id 20 and assert both edge endpoints resolve to known node ids after deserialisation.
items.minimumFixScope: Adjust the owned integration test data and assertions in crates/anvil-kernel-types/tests/type_invariants.rs.

items.title: Event type and payload pairing invariant is not exercised
items.recommendation: Add a helper/assertion that maps each EventType to the expected EventPayload variant and use it in the event tests, including coverage for all four event kinds. If mismatched events should be rejected, add a negative deserialisation or validation test around that contract.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tests only use valid examples and assert selected scalar fields; they do not check the type-to-payload relationship as a cross-type invariant.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a parameterised test over Progress, Snapshot, Violation, and Error events that round-trips each event and asserts the payload variant matches back.event_type.
items.minimumFixScope: Add event pairing assertions or a small test helper in crates/anvil-kernel-types/tests/type_invariants.rs.

items.title: `start --json` test accepts forbidden and wrong states
items.recommendation: Strengthen `start_json_emits_state_literal_in_status_verify_shape` to assert the concrete expected read-only fresh result, at minimum `state == "needs_action"` or the intended fresh JSON state, and explicitly reject `protecting`. Also assert the complete status-verify JSON key set if the contract is that the shape matches `anvil status --verify --json`.
items.reproduction: Change the JSON renderer or start command to emit `{"state":"protecting","headline":"x","config":"absent"}` for this path; this test would still pass despite violating the stated fresh-repo guardrail.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included JSON test is the intended coverage, but it only checks enum membership and three field types. The stronger human-output tests do not parse the JSON surface, so a JSON-only regression can pass.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Update `start_json_emits_state_literal_in_status_verify_shape` to assert exact state and all required LAUNCH-012 keys for a fresh temp repo/home, mirroring the status JSON contract test.
items.minimumFixScope: One integration test assertion update in `crates/anvil-cli/tests/start.rs`.

items.title: Dual-run harness never executes the TypeScript engine
items.recommendation: Wire run_dual to execute the real TS engine, or rename/scope the test as a scaffold until parity execution exists. Once integrated, remove the placeholder assertion and assert on known matching and intentionally divergent fixtures.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests codify the placeholder as expected behaviour and only verify Rust-only discrepancy reporting when the TS side is empty.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a fixture that both Rust and TS engines should evaluate identically, run both engines through run_dual, and assert matches is true with no discrepancies.
items.minimumFixScope: Replace the hard-coded empty ts_violations assignment in run_dual with a real TS-engine invocation and update the placeholder-specific test expectations.

items.title: Workspace-root containment is only integration-tested for read-only tools
items.recommendation: Add stdio integration tests for anvil_suppress and anvil_fix where the server is started in one tempdir, workspaceRoot points at a sibling tempdir, and the response is an error while the sibling file remains unchanged. Apply the same containment pattern to any other workspaceRoot-accepting or file-mutating MCP tool as it is added.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Existing out-of-root tests cover anvil_status and anvil_check only; the suppress and fix tests use spawn_mcp_server_in(workspace.path()) with workspaceRoot set to that same workspace, so they only prove the allowed path.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add mcp_serve_stdio_tools_call_suppress_rejects_workspace_outside_server_root and mcp_serve_stdio_tools_call_fix_rejects_workspace_outside_server_root using sibling tempdirs and unchanged-file assertions.
items.minimumFixScope: Extend crates/anvil-cli/tests/mcp_serve_stdio.rs with out-of-root negative cases for the write-capable workspaceRoot tools; if they fail, fix the corresponding MCP tool containment checks.

items.title: Lockfile hash test disables the entropy path it is meant to protect
items.recommendation: Run this case with entropy enabled, preferably with a threshold low enough to exercise the hash-like strings, and assert that no findings are returned for lockfile integrity and resolved hash lines.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This test is the only lockfile hash false-positive case in the owned file, but it disables entropy before scanning the high-entropy fixture.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Change does_not_flag_hex_hashes_in_lockfile to use config_with_entropy(...) and assert findings.is_empty() for the lockfile fixture.
items.minimumFixScope: Update crates/anvil-checks/tests/secret_detection.rs lockfile false-positive test configuration and assertion.

items.title: Air-gapped harness calls have no per-test timeout
items.recommendation: Run the harness through a bounded child process helper with a short timeout; on timeout, kill the child and fail the test with captured stdout/stderr and argv.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current clean-exit assertions are only reached after `cmd.output()` returns, so a hang prevents the assertion from executing.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Introduce a tiny test-only command or harness mode that sleeps past the timeout and assert the helper kills it and reports a timeout failure.
items.minimumFixScope: Replace blocking `cmd.output()` in both air-gapped helpers with a timeout-aware spawn/wait implementation or a small shared test utility.

items.title: Status air-gap coverage can pass despite attempted network work
items.recommendation: Tighten the status assertions to prove the local probe path was used: parse the JSON output and assert the expected local diagnostic shape, assert absence of network/auth/update error markers, or extend the harness to detect socket/connect attempts and fail on any such attempt.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests deliberately accept any exit code and do not inspect the successful local status payload or count network attempts.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a status fixture with expired credentials and assert `status --verify --json` returns the expected local activation diagnostic JSON while the harness reports zero socket/connect attempts.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `crates/anvil-cli/tests/air_gapped.rs` assertions and, if needed, the network-blocked harness contract to expose network-attempt detection.

items.title: Busy response assertion does not enforce JSON-RPC id echo
items.recommendation: Change the public busy assertion to take an expected id, or provide an `assert_busy_response_for(response, idx_or_id)` helper that validates `response["id"]` alongside the existing busy error shape.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The local integration test checks `contract-busy-99` separately after calling the public assertion, so the public helper's missing id check is not caught.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a unit test that passes a busy-shaped response with the wrong id to the public busy assertion and expects it to panic.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `assert_busy_response`'s signature or add a stricter companion helper, then update local and downstream callers.

items.title: Blocking-rule tests can leave parked workers when an assertion fails
items.recommendation: Wrap the blocking sections in a guard that releases the barrier on drop, or structure the tests so cleanup runs even when assertions panic. For async tests, a small RAII guard plus explicit disarm after normal release is enough.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests pass on the current implementation, so the panic cleanup path is never exercised.
items.minimumFixScope: Add panic-safe cleanup around `timing_out_rule_service` and `saturating_rule_service` users in this test file.

items.title: Shared contract API is trapped inside an integration test target
items.recommendation: Move the reusable request builders, assertions, fixture list, and helper services into a library-visible test-support module or small dev-support crate, then have `tests/midedit_contract.rs` import and exercise that API.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tests execute this file as its own integration test binary; they do not try to consume the fixture from another crate or integration-test target.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a consumer integration test in the intended downstream crate that imports the shared fixture API through the supported crate path and runs at least `run_full_contract`.
items.minimumFixScope: Expose the fixture API from a reusable crate/module and update this integration test to consume it.

items.title: Baseline suppression tests miss same-name symbol collisions
items.recommendation: Add collision fixtures with two distinct symbol IDs and different files but the same symbol name: mark the original as previously public or privileged, add the second symbol in the delta, and assert the expansion violation is still emitted for the new file/symbol identity. If the implementation fails, change baseline keys to include file and/or stable symbol identity rather than name alone.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing suppression tests contain only a single previously known symbol, and the mixed public baseline test uses `knownExport` versus `brandNewExport`, so no same-name collision path is exercised.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add `same_name_different_file_public_symbol_still_flags_new_export` and the analogous privileged-access test in `crates/anvil-kernel/tests/architecture_parity.rs`.
items.minimumFixScope: Extend `crates/anvil-kernel/tests/architecture_parity.rs`; if the new test fails, update GraphDelta baseline identity and the public/privilege invariant suppression checks.
